events.title: Grounded spec built
events.reasoning: The search across code, config, endpoints, and the PRD confirms Procol supports creating multi-stage sourcing events including RFQs, with capabilities for vendor invitations, awarding, and team-based user management, as documented in prd-procol-sourcing.md, catalog.json, and product-questionnaire.md. One concrete discrepancy emerged: the PRD specifies that phone fields should accept any 10-digit number, but the backend currently only checks length, not whether the input is actually digits, so values like "abcdefghij" could pass validation. This gap is worth testing because it could allow invalid phone data into vendor or user records.

deltas.prdSays: Accept any 10-digit number; reject malformed input politely (PRD §4.3, §5).
deltas.productDoes: The API checks phone LENGTH (rejects 9 or 11 digits) but NOT that characters are digits — it accepts a 10-char value containing letters. The frontend enforces digits-only, so the API is more lenient than the UI.

events.title: 2/2 flows enabled
events.reasoning: I matched the request against our catalog and identified two relevant flows for PROCOL DEMO: “Create event → surrogate bid → open award proposal” and “Create RFP + RFQ event (2-stage) and verify in DB.” I then validated both against the client’s live configuration and confirmed that both flows are enabled in this environment. Since all identified flows are available, I will proceed with executing both enabled flows to cover the requested scenarios.

events.title: 6/17 checks passed · 11 failed
events.reasoning: The end-to-end `events.surrogate_award` flow is confirmed working and DB-verified, but the overall run is red: 11 of 17 checks failed. One failure is a 5xx server error, so that needs engineering triage first because it signals a UAT platform or service issue. The other 10 are validation gaps, meaning the responses or data did not match the expected business rules, not that the system crashed. In short, the award path functions, but the surrounding contract and data-quality checks need fixes before this can be considered release-ready.

events.title: 9 product defect(s) confirmed by the Oracle · 11 of 17 checks failed
events.reasoning: Out of 17 field-aware automated checks run live on UAT for “Create a RFQ event” (PROCOL DEMO), 6 passed and 11 failed. The one 5xx server error is a definite defect, and the leading failure is [CHK-EVT-01] creating a draft event group with valid line items. The Oracle confirmed 9 defects from direct evidence—each tied to a failing request or a UI/API contradiction—so they are reproducible without assumptions. Notably, the end-to-end events.surrogate_award check passed with DB verification, meaning the award flow works while draft-event creation needs fixing.
